newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wuhan Store completes big retail complex.
newsitem.headline: Wuhan Store completes big retail complex.

text.p: Wuhan Department Store (Group) Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it had completed the construction of a one billion yuan retail complex in Wuhan, the capital of central China's Hubei province.
The project was completed two months ahead of schedule and would go into partial operation on September 28, a company spokesman told the China Securities Bulletin.

Shenzhen-listed Wuhan Store had a 51 percent-stake in the 173,000-sq-metre Wuhan Plaza, which contains retail, office and residential space, as well as restaurants and entertainment facilities, the spokesman said.
The remaining 49 percent was held by a Hong Kong-based company, he added.
Upon full operations next year, the complex should generate pre-tax earnings of about 100 million yuan on sales of 1.5 billion yuan annually, the spokesman said.

Wuhan Store said in its interim report that under Chinese accounting standards, it had net profits of 26.46 million yuan in the first half of 1996, compared with 42.68 million yuan in the same period of last year.
The company blamed the earnings plunge on a steep slide in revenue from its real estate sector. It gave no details.
The retailer reported after-tax profits of 81.01 million yuan for 1995, down 41 percent from 136.52 million yuan a year earlier.
The firm said operations last year were seriously hurt by a shortage of funds caused by Beijing's tight monetary policy.
